visualReview.notes: Compared the three open porticoes, stepped shikharas, curved stone courses and standalone pavilion with Yazdani’s original Archaeological Department photographs and measured plan. Inspected the corrected north and south porticoes from the forecourt and both approaches.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Reviewed the dark basalt plinth, finely layered carving bands, open pillared portals and pale plaster shikharas in the shared scene. Geographic placement loaded and unloaded.

mediumFiReview.notes: Four levels retain the two distinct pale spires, projecting porticoes and west pavilion. Street and close-up views carry the recessed niches, animal friezes and turned pillar capitals. The skyline roofs close continuously from the eaves to the finials.

terrain.grade: The original Copernicus GLO-30 field is 200 metres across and ranges from 453.0015 to 465.5195 m EGM2008. The forecourt datum is 457.2689 m. The platform and all stairs meet the original field.

geographicReview.notes: The named OpenStreetMap node 13313260103 and the current building roof outline locate the measured historical footprint, its three entrances and the freestanding pavilion. The placement agrees with the front court and surrounding site grade.

fidelityReview.scope: The standing dark-stone Aundha Nagnath temple with three porticoes, star-shaped halls, the rebuilt white shikhara and the Nandi pavilion immediately outside the historical western entrance.
fidelityReview.notes: The temple and west pavilion follow the original measured plan. Relief sculpture, stair risers and individual roof course offsets are approximated. The model covers the temple and pavilion.

imageryReview.notes: Checked the published Qualla gallery first. The original public-domain exterior, carvings and shikhara photographs were published in the Archaeological Department’s 1918 report. The measured plan was published by the same department in 1919.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Reviewed the approach and pavilion, plinth carving, roof profiles, mapped footprint, all four detail levels and the original terrain field.

limitations: Draft exterior: approximate photographic proportions and simplified ornament. It is not a survey, photogrammetric reconstruction or approved current geographic replacement.
The exact 1918 photographs define the dark stone courses, entry piers and white shikhara. The current district survey records the later tower at about sixty feet.
Terrain sampling/contact, geographic alignment and site activation remain pending. Runtime LODs are produced by the registered after-import pipeline and require visual review.
Reference photos remain in the local Qualla corpus; only provenance, paths and hashes are retained here.
